input.quote: iii. Licensor hereby, subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement and provided that Licensee makes payments to Licensor as required under this Agreement, grants to Licensee a non-exclusive license to utilize Licensed Technology solely in the Field of Use and subject to the additional restrictions set forth below and otherwise in this License Agreement.
input.rationale: The grant in p0030 runs to Licensee alone, and p0045 (read with p0041/p0042 and Article VI at p0085) bars access by anyone other than Licensee's own employees, so Affiliates and contractors acting for us are excluded with only a discretionary Licensor-consent path — short of even the fallback (Affiliates covered on written notice). Transferability also fails the fallback: p0149 bars assignment without Licensor's consent with no successor/M&A carve-out, and Article XX (p0134) auto-terminates the licence on a Change of Control absent consent, which Licensor is deemed reasonable to withhold whenever it "reasonably believes" its interests are adversely affected. We therefore propose the minimal preferred edits: extend the grant to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, conform the employee-only restriction, and add a consent-free successor transfer right; Affiliate use on written notice remains an acceptable fallback. The licence is not revocable at will on its face (36-month initial term), so we have not addressed the no-cure termination right in Article IV under this rule.

proposal.summary: Extend licence grant to Licensee's Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf and permit transfer to a successor
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have extended the grant to our Affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf, and added a successor-transfer right, because our playbook requires the licence to cover the group and personnel who actually operate the Platform for us and to survive an internal reorganisation or M&A transaction. As a fallback we can accept Affiliate use on written notice to Licensor.
